title: Midquarter exec bridge and prioritization scenario plan
content:
Purpose:
This is the mid‑quarter 'bridge' doc to prepare the exec update and the company all‑hands. It synthesizes: (a) a compact OKR rebase for the next six weeks, (b) three decision scenarios with triggers and owners, and (c) a short communications plan and slide checklist for the exec update + all‑hands.

Context / why now:
- We finished a capacity reforecast after Dedicated demand came in higher than expected; finance flagged a potential Q2 overrun if we don't slow a handful of non‑critical workstreams.
- Product has an important feature milestone (streaming tool-calls) that promises go-to-market lift but risks platform SLO if rushed.
- Leadership asked for a concise set of scenarios and recommended tradeoffs to choose from in the next exec sync (Mar 2).

Summary recommendation (topline):
- Present 3 scenarios to execs and ask for a directional decision during the meeting. My recommended default is Scenario B (balanced): pause non‑urgent infra tech debt, accelerate streaming feature with canary + gating, and allocate a short-term Dedicated burst to cover expected throughput for 6 weeks.

OKR rebase (draft):
- Objective 1: Keep customer-facing latency stable while supporting GTM feature launches.
  - KR1: P95 inference latency <= 250ms for hosted API (target window: next 6 weeks)
  - KR2: No more than 1 production rollback related to model-serving regressions (6 weeks)
  - KR3: Deliver streaming tool-calls canary to 10 pilot customers by end of run (6 weeks)

- Objective 2: Bring unit costs down to protect margin during Q2 spike.
  - KR1: Implement prefix-KV cache for top 5 customers (measured unit cost reduction >= 8%)
  - KR2: Deploy quantized variant for two large models in infra pool (cost delta validated on staging)

Decision scenarios (one pager):
A) Accelerate GTM (Aggressive)
  - What we do: Move full engineering focus to streaming tool-calls + GTM. Pause non-customer-facing infra work for 8 weeks. Approve immediate Dedicated burst for throughput.
  - Signals to pick this: Sales pipeline conversion > $1.2M ARR expected from pilot customers; marketing time-to-market critical; customer pilots with NDAs ready.
  - Risks: Increased operational risk for platform SLOs; potential cost overrun if Dedicated burst not sized correctly.
  - Owners: Product (Samira) + Eng (Diego) + Finance (Priya).

B) Balanced (Recommended)
  - What we do: Prioritize streaming canary + safe rollout (canary gating, rollback hooks). Defer non-critical infra engineering by 40% capacity. Approve limited Dedicated burst (4–6 weeks) with clear burn rate cap.
  - Signals to pick this: Moderate pipeline lift expected (~$600–900k), finance okay with short burst, pilot customers willing to accept pilot class.
  - Risks: Slower feature reach than A; slightly higher short-term unit cost.
  - Owners: Product (Samira) + Eng (Diego) + Platform (Ola).

C) Protect platform (Conservative)
  - What we do: Hold product feature pace, fully prioritize platform reliability, accelerate cache/quantization work. No Dedicated burst; rely on routing fallbacks and throttling.
  - Signals to pick this: Finance refuses extra spend; SRE incident rate > threshold; legal/compliance blocker on pilot.
  - Risks: Missed GTM opportunity and slower pipeline conversion.
  - Owners: SRE (Ola) + Platform (Diego) + Finance (Priya).

Decision slate (for exec meeting):
- Vote for scenario A / B / C + optional Qs: (1) Approve Dedicated burst? (2) Approve temporary reallocation of 40% infra squad time?
- Decision thresholds suggested: Dedicated burst approved only if finance signs off on < 10% incremental Q2 spend; canary go/no-go gated on staging perf checks (latency and mem usage).

Signals / telemetry to show in the meeting (one slide each):
1) Latency trend (P50/P95) for hosted API the last 8 weeks (highlight anomalies tied to major deploys)
2) Cost forecast (burn vs plan) with Dedicated burst scenarios overlaid (3 lines)
3) Sales pipeline uplift estimate from pilot customers (qualitative + quantitative)
4) Risk heatmap (SRE incidents, infra debt list, compliance flags)

Execution checklist (owner + ETA):
- Slides for exec update: 6 slides total (objective, scenarios + recommendation, telemetry, finance impact, risk map, ask). Owner: Avery. ETA: Mar 1 0900 PT.
- All‑hands talking points and TL;DR email: short script + FAQs. Owner: Samira. ETA: Mar 3 1200 PT.
- Engineering briefs: canary rollout plan + rollback criteria doc (GH PR). Owner: Diego. ETA: Feb 25 EOD.
- Finance signoff: commit to burst cap and monitoring. Owner: Priya. ETA: Feb 28 EOD.

Communications plan (exec -> company):
- Exec sync (Mar 2): decision and directional guidance.
- All‑hands (Mar 4): CEO high-level narrative + Product demo clip (30s) + Ops explanation of why choices were made. Keep the message: "Prioritizing customer outcomes while protecting reliability."
- Follow-up email: 3 bullets (what changed, why, what to expect) + link to read‑only FAQ page. Owner: Communications.

Slide checklist (quick):
- Slide 1: One-line theme + ask
- Slide 2: 6-week goals and rebase OKRs
- Slide 3: Scenarios summary table (A/B/C) with recommended pick
- Slide 4: Telemetry (latency/cost/pipeline)
- Slide 5: Risks & mitigations
- Slide 6: Clear asks (budget + time reallocation + go/no-go gate)

Open questions / things to resolve before the exec meeting:
- Exact burst sizing: Ops needs expected QPS for pilot; ask Sales to enumerate pilot customer expected traffic (JIRA: INF-2026).
- Cache rollout prioritization: which customers in top-5 list will be easiest? (Product to confirm)
- Communication for customers on Dedicated vs Hosted: Draft note required for account teams.

Notes to self / rough todo list (informal):
- [ ] Pull latency graphs from observability (Ola)
- [ ] Draft slide 3 scenario comparison table (Avery)
- [ ] Confirm finance cap language and emergency cut-off (Priya)
- [ ] Prep two-line reactive script for CEO for all-hands Q&A

Appendix (useful links):
- Confluence OKR draft: confluence.redwood/infr/OKR-Q2-2026-draft
- Staging perf runbook: github.com/redwood/infra/ops/runbooks/staging-perf.md
- Jira epic: https://jira.redwood/browse/INF-2026

Tone guidance for slides: concise, evidence-first, one recommended path with fallback. Avoid technical deep‑dives on the first slide; put those in backup slides.

If you want to iterate on language for the all‑hands TL;DR email, I have three short variants below (pick one for final):
1) "This week we decided to prioritize a controlled rollout of streaming tool-calls while protecting latency for customers. Expect a phased pilot with clear rollback criteria and a short-term capacity increase to support trials."
2) "We’re focusing on shipping a critical product pilot while keeping our platform solid. We’ll use a limited capacity boost and canary gating to reduce risk. More details at the all-hands."
3) "Our priority is customer impact: shipping the pilot for a better product experience while taking deliberate steps to protect reliability and cost."

---
End of draft.

Feedback requested: please comment inline on the scenarios (are we missing a tradeoff?), and add any metrics you want in the telemetry slide.
